mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in RSAFS (personal savings) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a shift toward higher borrowing and spending, which can temporarily boost consumer demand and support S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month AND RSAFS < previous month - 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in GDPC1 and HOUST above their respective 3-month moving averages signals strengthening housing and overall demand, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals persistent employment weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises above 3% and FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, it indicates inflation without a corresponding policy response, eroding real earnings and pushing equities lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
